correctness.rationale: For n≥2, H≤F2^n acts freely on cube vertices with coset orbits x+H. In inclusive distance-two Rips, a coset spans a simplex iff max_{h∈H}wt(h)≤2; otherwise no geometric fixed point (orbit-barycenter model). If all nonzero H weights≤2, a basis-weight argument forces rank≤2: a weight-one e_i plus an independent vector yields a coordinate two-plane; otherwise independent weight-two vectors overlap in one coordinate and span the even-weight three-coordinate plane, no further independent vector has weight≤2 across the full span. For rank2 two different cosets cannot coexist in an allowable simplex because some cross-coset pair has wt≥3; hence exactly 2^(n−2) isolated fixed barycenters. For rank1 generated by wt1, quotient cosets labelled F2^(n−1) join iff their labels differ in one bit, exactly the graph Q_(n−1), with no 2-simplices. For generator wt2, quotient Cayley graph generators (1,0),(1,e_j) form an F2 basis, again Q_(n−1). Graph Euler β1=1+(n−3)2^(n−2), including n=2 interval. Independent exhaustive binary-subspace/coset enumeration for n=2..5 found 4,15,66,373 nontrivial subgroup cases with the exact cube/discrete/empty types. Source verifier code inspected for further n=6 and special n=7,8 claims, not trusted as infinite proof.
